title: Consider downloading rather than rendering resources delivered over FTP.
body:
Chrome is interested in downloading rather than rendering FTP resources, as another step towards getting rid of FTP completely (there's discussion on blink-dev@ at https://groups.google.com/a/chromium.org/forum/#!topic/blink-dev/eopgOoY1QLs, opinions are welcome!).

I've heard some interest from Mozilla folks (@ckerschb, @dveditz, @jonathanKingston, and @valenting). I'm not exactly sure how to specify this suggestion, as Fetch leaves FTP as an exercise for the reader, and HTML doesn't differentiate between protocols in its navigation algorithms.

The implementation in https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/1337338/ accomplishes this by forcing FTP resources to have a `binary/octet-stream` MIME type, unless it's a user-agent-generated directory listing, which has a MIME type of `text/vnd.chromium.ftp-dir` (it looks like Firefox uses a different type for its generated page: [`text/ftp-dir`](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/source/netwerk/protocol/ftp/nsFtpConnectionThread.cpp#1174)). We further disable MIME sniffing for `ftp:` resources.

One approach could be to add an additional step to HTML's "[process a navigate response](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#process-a-navigate-response)" algorithm, around the `Content-Disposition` check in step 3. Perhaps:

> 3.  If _response_'s URL's scheme is "`ftp`", **and it is not a user-agent-rendered directory listing**, then handle it as a download and return.

The directory listing bit is more than a little hand-wavey.

An alternative approach could modify Fetch to add an (equally hand-wavey) note to the `ftp` entry in [scheme fetch](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-scheme-fetch) regarding the expected MIME type of any response, and altering the MIME type list in step 5 of HTML's "[process a navigate response](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#process-a-navigate-response)" algorithm to handle whatever MIME type we specified in Fetch as a download?

WDYT?
